compensating.why: hop 2 leaves out the PAX global extended header
hop 3 leaves out the GNU long-name entry
hop 1 answers from the file only if the file exists

ownership_reason: Only the gold makes the header decision for an entry that was not created from a file: the directory link flag, the header kinds and the name. Hop 1 only answers for an entry created from a file (an entry read from an archive never is one) and hops 2-4 hand the entry and its link flag on unchanged, so once the gold reports a PAX extended header whose name ends with a slash as a directory, TarArchiveInputStream reads none of its data and parses its records as the next header. The gold's javadoc promises whether the entry represents a directory; a PAX header is a header entry whose data are records for the next entry, not a directory. The convention is pinned outside the gold: TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry reads a PAX header entry's data as PAX records (paxHeaders, readGlobalPaxHeaders); TarArchiveOutputStream.writePaxHeaders names its PAX entries through stripTo7Bits, whose shouldBeReplaced replaces '/' so that the PAX header is not considered a directory, and writes the PAX data with a size that putArchiveEntry honours only for a non-directory. survivesBlankLinesInPaxHeader, testWriteNonAsciiDirectoryNamePosixMode and testWriteSimplePaxHeaders (PAX headers through the chain) and testWriteLongDirectoryNameTruncateMode (the link-flag side through the chain) pass.
